text: Correcting myself within the hour. I reported that the size fix was working on the strength of one reading of 0.541 -- which was simply the mean of the three stocks I had just seeded, read back to me by a watcher script that had frozen on its first sample. A direct probe says size is 0.075 at year 15,270, back at the floor within forty-two years, and energy is 11.1 against a bar of 20.8. The fix did not work, and it could not have: it was mathematically incapable of working. Here is why, and it matters more than the fix. Intake is take = min(bite, avail*graze), and with flora around 1,650 spread over 21,000 cells there is roughly 0.08 biomass per cell -- so the availability term is the binding one everywhere, and the bite term never applies. In that regime intake does not depend on body size at all, while basal cost still scales as size^0.75. digest_size_gain only multiplies the ENERGY EXTRACTED from whatever was taken, so with min a and gain b the return per unit cost is (a+b*s)/s^0.75, which is increasing only where s > 3a/b. With a=0.70 and b=1.30 that is s > 1.615, and size cannot exceed 1.0. There is no value of digest_size_gain that makes body mass pay while intake is availability-capped. So I was fixing the wrong half. The half that matters is the cap itself, and the code has a mechanism for it sitting four lines above the one I changed: a large grazer reaching into the four neighbouring cells, reach = clip((size - reach_size_min)/reach_size_span, 0, 1). reach_size_min is 99.0. Size maxes at 1.0, so reach is identically zero and the branch never runs. The comment directly above it reads: 'Per-tick intake capped at one cell's biomass is what drives every lineage to the size floor: basal cost rises with mass but the meal does not, so nothing stays big enough to be prey and the predator tier has nobody to eat.' That is the third extinction described in advance, and it is the second mechanism I have now found written, documented, wired in and switched off by a sentinel -- digest_size_gain at 0.0 and reach_size_min at 99.0, both aimed at this exact failure, both disabled. Setting reach_size_min 0.0 and reach_size_span 0.7 makes availability scale from one cell to five across the size range. Combined with the digestion term already in place the return per unit cost runs 9.3 at size 0.05, dipping to 6.9 at 0.15, then 7.6 at 0.35, 9.2 at 0.55 and 10.5 at 0.70. There is still a shallow valley near the floor, which is honest -- a small-bodied strategy should remain viable -- but it is no longer the only one, and the optimum is now at 0.7 instead of at the floor. The surviving animals are at 0.075 and sit below the valley, so I am seeding 400 at 0.60 on the upslope; if size climbs rather than falls over the next two hundred years, that is the answer, and it is also the first time this world will have had anything big enough to be worth hunting. Watch tps: the reach branch costs four gathers and four scatters per tick and has never run before.
